# `node_resource`

`node_resource` measures one resource of the whole node: its CPU, its
memory, its swap space, its load, the time that its processors wait for a
disk, its memory pressure, or its open files.
MMWatchdog reads the resource measurements from the kernel's own files
below `/proc` and runs no program to obtain the resource measurements.
The value of the check is the name of the resource, such as
`node_resource: memory`.

A `node_resource` check only measures. The limit is written beside the
module, in `fail_when_measurement_above` or `fail_when_measurement_below`,
and MMWatchdog applies it in the same way as for every module that measures
([checks that measure a number](../configuration-files.md#checks-that-measure)).
With `only_record_readings: true`, the check only records its readings.

Use a related module for other resources:
[`node_filesystem`](node_filesystem.md) for the space of one
filesystem, [`node_disk_device`](node_disk_device.md) for one disk,
[`node_network_interface`](node_network_interface.md) for one network
interface, and [`systemd_unit_resource`](systemd_unit_resource.md) for
the CPU, the memory, or the processes of one systemd unit.

## Inputs

The module takes one value, which a check writes after the module's name, and no other input.

- the value of `node_resource` (`cpu`, `memory`, `swap`, `load`, `io_wait`, `memory_pressure`, or `open_files`; required): The resource to measure.

## Measurements

- `cpu_used_percent` (percent): For cpu: the share of the node's processor time that was in use since the run before.
- `memory_used_percent` (percent): For memory: the share of the node's memory that is not available to programs.
- `swap_used_percent` (percent): For swap: the share of the swap space that is in use. A node without swap space uses 0.
- `load_average_1m` (load): For load: the kernel's load average over 1 minute. load_average_5m and load_average_15m are the same over 5 and 15 minutes.
- `load_average_1m_per_core` (load per core): For load: the load average over 1 minute for each processor of the node. load_average_5m_per_core and load_average_15m_per_core are the same over 5 and 15 minutes.
- `io_wait_percent` (percent): For io_wait: the share of the processors' time since the run before in which they had nothing to run because programs waited for a disk.
- `memory_pressure_percent` (percent): For memory_pressure: the share of the last 60 seconds in which at least one program had to wait for memory.
- `open_files_used_percent` (percent): For open_files: the open files of the whole machine, as a share of the kernel's limit.

A check sets a limit on a measurement with `fail_when_measurement_above` or `fail_when_measurement_below`, and fails when a reading passes its limit. A check that only records its readings states `only_record_readings: true`, no limit, and no `alert_severity`; it never alerts. The configuration files reference explains limits in [checks that measure a number](../configuration-files.md#checks-that-measure).

## When the check fails, and when it cannot check

- **The check fails** when a reading passes one of its limits. A reading
  strictly above its `fail_when_measurement_above` number, or strictly
  below its `fail_when_measurement_below` number, fails the check; an equal
  reading passes. The check then fails at its `alert_severity`.
  The check's incident follows the check group's
  [failing time](../../how-to/decide-when-a-check-alerts.md).
- **A check with `only_record_readings: true` only records, never fails,
  never alerts, and takes no `alert_severity`**
  ([checks that only record](../../how-to/look-back-at-measurements.md)).
  A reading that MMWatchdog cannot make shows as unknown in
  `mmwatchdog status`, and opens no incident.
- **MMWatchdog cannot check** when MMWatchdog cannot make a reading.
  The run's result, called an observation, is then unknown, with the reason,
  and never a reading of zero. An unknown result of a check that can alert
  opens a separate cannot-check incident after `alert_after_failing_for`
  ([scheduling and observed state](../../changing-mmwatchdog/design/checks.md#scheduling-and-observed-state)).
  The causes are listed under [errors](#errors-and-what-they-mean).
- **A limit on a measurement that this run could not make** makes the
  observation unknown, with the reason. The one case in which a resource
  has only some of its measurements is `load`: without the number of
  processors, the three `_per_core` measurements are missing.

### The commands that use the most of a resource

When a check of `cpu`, `memory`, `swap`, or `load` fails, the body of its
alert names the five programs that use the most of that resource, by name
and process ID:

```text
memory_used_percent is 94.2 (fails above 90)
failing since 14:02 UTC
the commands that use the most memory:
  3051 MiB: mysqld (process 812)
  640 MiB: python3 (process 2210)
  212 MiB: systemd-journald (process 301)
  96 MiB: nginx (process 955)
  95 MiB: nginx (process 956)
```

| Resource | The first line of the list | What each line gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memory` | `the commands that use the most memory:` | The memory of the process that is in physical memory, in MiB |
| `swap` | `the commands that use the most swap space:` | The memory of the process that is in swap space, in MiB, from `VmSwap` in `/proc/PROCESS_ID/status` |
| `cpu` | `the commands that used the most CPU between the two CPU readings:` | The processor time that the process used in the time of the reading, as a percent of the whole node, like `cpu_used_percent` itself, such as `41.5 percent` |
| `load` | `the commands with the most threads that run or wait for a disk now:` | The process's count of threads that run or wait for a disk now, such as `3 threads`. The load average counts threads that run or wait for a disk, over a longer time |

- Each line is one process: the name of its program, without the
  arguments, and its process ID. The arguments are left out because they
  can hold a password or a token, and the alert goes to every destination
  that takes it. To see a whole command line, run
  `ps -o args= -p PROCESS_ID` on the node while the process runs. A process
  without a command line, such as a thread of the kernel, shows its name in
  brackets, such as `[kswapd0]`. The highest amount comes first.
  MMWatchdog leaves out processes that use none of the resource or end
  in the meantime.
- MMWatchdog reads the commands in every run in which the check fails, so the alert
  has the commands from the run that confirmed the failure. `mmwatchdog status CHECK_GROUP` and
  `mmwatchdog check-now CHECK_GROUP` also show the resource-use command
  list for a failed check. JSON has the resource-use command list as `details` of the observation
  ([title and body of an alert](../alert-format.md)).
- A check that only records, and a check that is within its limit, names no
  command. A check of `io_wait`, `memory_pressure`, or `open_files` names
  none either.

## Examples

### Limits on the CPU, the memory, the swap space, and the load

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/check_groups/machine.yml
check_groups:
  machine:
    check_every: 30s
    time_limit_per_run: 5s
    alert_after_failing_for: 10m
    recovered_after_healthy_for: 5m
    checks:
      cpu_use_is_recorded:
        only_record_readings: true
        node_resource: cpu                        # no limit: records only, never alerts
      memory_is_below_90_percent:
        node_resource: memory
        fail_when_measurement_above:
          memory_used_percent: 90
        alert_severity: warn
      swap_is_below_50_percent:
        node_resource: swap
        fail_when_measurement_above:
          swap_used_percent: 50
        alert_severity: info
      load_average_5m_per_core_is_below_1_5:
        node_resource: load
        fail_when_measurement_above:
          load_average_5m_per_core: 1.5
        alert_severity: warn
```

Every 30 seconds, MMWatchdog on the node runs the four checks:

1. `cpu_use_is_recorded` measures the share of the node's processor time
   that was in use since its run before, and stores the reading in the
   node's [measurement history](../../how-to/look-back-at-measurements.md).
   `cpu_use_is_recorded` never alerts.
2. `memory_is_below_90_percent` fails when more than 90 percent of the
   node's memory is in use. Once `memory_is_below_90_percent` has failed
   for 10 minutes, MMWatchdog sends a
   `warn` alert whose body names the five commands that use the most
   memory.
3. `swap_is_below_50_percent` fails when more than half of the swap space
   is in use, and alerts at `info`.
4. `load_average_5m_per_core_is_below_1_5` fails when the 5-minute load
   average, divided by the number of processors, is above 1.5. A limit of
   1.5 on `load_average_5m_per_core` suits a node with 2 processors and
   a node with 64.

Each check is healthy again after 5 minutes within the check's limit,
and MMWatchdog then sends the recovery alert.

### Signs that the machine is in trouble

Three more resources say that the machine is in trouble before a program
fails:

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/check_groups/machine_health.yml
check_groups:
  machine_health:
    check_every: 30s
    time_limit_per_run: 5s
    alert_after_failing_for: 10m
    recovered_after_healthy_for: 5m
    checks:
      io_wait_is_below_30_percent:
        node_resource: io_wait
        fail_when_measurement_above:
          io_wait_percent: 30
        alert_severity: warn
      memory_pressure_is_below_10_percent:
        node_resource: memory_pressure
        fail_when_measurement_above:
          memory_pressure_percent: 10
        alert_severity: warn
      open_files_are_below_80_percent:
        node_resource: open_files
        fail_when_measurement_above:
          open_files_used_percent: 80
        alert_severity: warn
```

- **`io_wait_percent`** is the usual first sign of a slow or failing disk.
  The check fails when the processors spent more than 30 percent of their
  time since the run before waiting for a disk, with nothing else to run.
- **`memory_pressure_percent`** says that the machine is short of memory
  right now. The check fails when, in more than
  10 percent of the last 60 seconds, at least one program had to wait for
  memory. Swap space that was filled during an earlier peak and is still
  in use does not raise
  `memory_pressure_percent`. Limit `memory_pressure_percent` where a
  limit on swap would alert for no reason.
- **`open_files_used_percent`** fails above 80 percent of the kernel's
  limit on open files. A machine that reaches the limit cannot open a file
  or accept a connection.

## How it works

Each run reads one resource from the kernel's files:

| Resource | Measurements | Where MMWatchdog reads each resource, and how it counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpu` | `cpu_used_percent` | From `/proc/stat`: busy time divided by total time across all processors since the previous run. Idle, I/O wait, and stolen time are not busy. Guest time is not counted twice. A decrease in the I/O wait counter contributes zero to the interval, as the [kernel's documentation of `/proc/stat`](https://docs.kernel.org/filesystems/proc.html#miscellaneous-kernel-statistics-in-proc-stat) allows. Any other backward counter needs a new sample. 0 to 100 |
| `memory` | `memory_used_percent` | `/proc/meminfo`: 100 × (1 − `MemAvailable` / `MemTotal`), the share of the physical memory that is not available to programs. 0 to 100 |
| `swap` | `swap_used_percent` | `/proc/meminfo`: 100 × (1 − `SwapFree` / `SwapTotal`). A node without swap space reads 0. 0 to 100 |
| `load` | `load_average_1m`, `load_average_5m`, `load_average_15m`, and each with `_per_core` | `/proc/loadavg`: the kernel's load average over 1, 5, and 15 minutes, 0 or more. A `_per_core` measurement, such as `load_average_5m_per_core`, divides the load average by the number of online logical CPUs listed in `/proc/stat` |
| `io_wait` | `io_wait_percent` | The same counters of `/proc/stat` as `cpu`: the share of the processors' time since the run before in which they had nothing to run because programs waited for a disk. 0 to 100 |
| `memory_pressure` | `memory_pressure_percent` | `/proc/pressure/memory`: the `avg60` value of the line `some`, the share of the last 60 seconds in which at least one program had to wait for memory. 0 to 100 |
| `open_files` | `open_files_used_percent` | `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr`: subtract the unused kernel file handles from the allocated kernel file handles, then divide by the kernel's file-handle limit. Multiply by 100 to get the percentage of kernel file handles in use. 0 to 100 |

- **`cpu` and `io_wait` measure over a time.** A reading covers the time
  since the check's run before. The first run takes a fresh sample of
  200 ms. A run after a counter went backwards or after the number of
  processors changed also takes a fresh sample.
  A fresh sample is also needed after a gap longer than
  `2 × check_every + time_limit_per_run` between samples.
  So the check group's
  `time_limit_per_run` must be longer than `200ms`.

  The message ends with the time that the reading covers,
  such as `cpu_used_percent is 12.5 (fails above 80) over 30.000s`. The
  [CPU sampling](../configuration-files.md#readings-over-a-time) section of the configuration
  files reference gives the rules that every module that measures a rate shares.
- **`memory`, `swap`, `load`, `memory_pressure`, and `open_files` are read
  at the moment of the run.** The load averages and the memory pressure
  are averages that the kernel keeps
  itself; MMWatchdog does not average them again.
- **The message** names each measurement that has a limit,
  with its reading and its limit, such as `memory_used_percent is 41.27
  (fails above 90)`. A check without a limit names every reading: a check of `load`
  names all six.
- **The commands for the alert** are read only by a check that has a limit
  and an `alert_severity`. For `memory`, `swap`, and `load`, MMWatchdog reads
  the resource-use command list only in a run that fails.
  For `cpu`, MMWatchdog reads the processor time of every
  process at the start and end of every reading. The command list covers
  the time that `cpu_used_percent` covers; a process that started during the reading
  counts with all the processor time that it has used.

## Errors and what they mean

Each validation error starts with the file, the line, and the path of the
setting, such as `check_groups.machine.checks.memory_is_below_90_percent.node_resource:`.

- **`must be one of cpu, memory, swap, load, io_wait, memory_pressure,
  open_files`.** The value names no resource that MMWatchdog measures. The space of
  a filesystem is a [`node_filesystem`](node_filesystem.md) check.
- **`this check has no such measurement; it measures memory_used_percent`.**
  A limit names a measurement of another resource. Each resource has only
  the measurements listed in the resource's row of the table above.
- **`expected a number from 0 to 100`** for a limit on a `_percent`
  measurement, and **`expected a number of 0 or more`** for a limit on a
  load average.
- **`a node_resource check needs a limit to alert`.** Add a measurement limit,
  or replace the severity with `only_record_readings: true`.

- **`time_limit_per_run: must exceed 200ms for the initial CPU sample`.** A
  check of `cpu` or `io_wait` needs more time than its first sample.

When MMWatchdog cannot make a reading, the observation is unknown with one of these
messages:

- **`the kernel of this machine does not provide the memory pressure
  (/proc/pressure/memory)`.** The kernel was built or started without
  memory pressure accounting. If the kernel supports memory pressure
  accounting but disables memory pressure accounting by default,
  the boot option `psi=1` enables memory pressure accounting.
  Otherwise limit `memory_used_percent`
  on such a machine instead. The kernels of Rocky Linux 9 and AlmaLinux 9
  are built this way: run `grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=psi=1` and
  restart the machine once.
- **`CPU counters changed or did not advance between samples; MMWatchdog waits for a new sample`.** Even the fresh sample of 200 ms gave no reading: the
  counters of `/proc/stat` went backwards, did not move, or the number of
  processors changed. The next run takes a new sample.
- **`the number of processors is unavailable:`** followed by the reason.
  A check of `load` has a limit on a `_per_core` measurement, and MMWatchdog could
  not read `/proc/stat`.
- **A message that names a file of `/proc`,** such as `/proc/meminfo:
  MemAvailable unavailable`, or `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr: expected three
  numbers`. The kernel's file is missing or has a form that MMWatchdog does not
  know.
- **`cpu_used_percent measurement is invalid`,** with the name of the
  measurement. A reading was negative or not a number, which MMWatchdog never
  reports as a value.

## Tested on

- **Go tests** in `internal/checksandalerts`: `resources_test.go` covers the
  limits, the CPU counters and sampling, the readings of swap and load, and
  a check whose limit was removed; `node_measurements_test.go` covers the
  readings of the I/O wait, the memory pressure, and the open files, also
  on a kernel without memory pressure. `processes_test.go` in
  `internal/primitives` covers the commands in the alert of each resource.
  On Linux, `resources_linux_test.go` in `internal/daemon` verifies that
  `mmwatchdog check-now` leaves the CPU baseline of the scheduled runs alone.
- **On real guests**, the suite `resources.py` tests recording the node's
  CPU, memory, swap, and load, including per-core load, without limits.
  Limits on the CPU and memory open incidents.

  `node_scenarios.py` measures the I/O wait and the memory pressure of the
  guest's kernel, compares the open files with `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr`, and
  checks the message of a kernel without memory pressure where the guest
  has none. The suite `node_scenarios.py` also fails
  checks of the memory and the CPU with a program that holds 96 MiB and a
  program that keeps a processor busy. The suite finds the memory program
  in the alert body and the CPU program in an observation's command list.
  A check of the load that fails in the same moment names the busy
  program too.
- The suites `resources.py` and `node_scenarios.py` and the Go tests passed on
  [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution)
  in the latest run of the whole catalog
  ([validation record](../../changing-mmwatchdog/validation.md)).

## Why it works this way

- **Recording readings is an explicit choice.** State
  `only_record_readings: true` to record readings without alerts or recovery.
  A missing severity must not silently turn an intended alert into readings only.

- **MMWatchdog applies the limit, and the module only measures.** Every module
  takes limits in a uniform way, and every reading reaches the
  measurement history
  ([check group decisions](../../changing-mmwatchdog/design/checks.md#check-group-decisions)).
- **A check without a limit never alerts.** A busy machine is not a
  failure until the operator sets a limit.
- **A reading that cannot be made is unknown, never zero.** A zero would
  look like a healthy machine.
- **Levels are two checks.** A `warn` at 80 percent and an `sos` at 95
  percent are two checks with two limits. MMWatchdog has no per-measurement
  setting that raises alert severity when a reading crosses a second limit.
- **The load is also measured per core.** One limit then suits machines of
  every size.
- **The memory pressure is a resource of its own.** A limit on the swap
  space alerts on a machine that filled its swap in an earlier peak and is
  healthy now; the memory pressure only rises while programs wait.
- **`io_wait` keeps the kernel's name.** `io_wait` is the word that
  operators know and search for.
- **The alert names the commands.** The first question about full memory
  or a busy processor is which program caused the high resource use.
  MMWatchdog includes the resource-use command list in the alert so
  operators can identify the programs without logging in to the node.
  The command list has no setting and is not given for filesystems.
